top3.headline: The Jensen Huang story gets worse, says Stratechery
top3.whyItMatters: Nvidia leadership risk is still growing; know how much your AI plans depend on one supplier.

top3.headline: AI 2027 authors pull their top-researcher AI forecast into 2027
top3.whyItMatters: People closest to the labs are shortening timelines; revisit plans that assume slow change.

top3.headline: Dharmesh Shah: AI startups win by staying off the labs' path
top3.whyItMatters: Labs need to sell tokens, so companies with domain and distribution can profit from them.

items.title: Ryan Carson built a custom Duolingo for his wife in one day
items.takeaway: Her feature requests ship within an hour; he says personal software is here.
items.soWhat: When one person can build a bespoke tool in a day, buy-versus-build math changes.

items.title: Theo rethinks his Gemini 4 Carbon verdict after more tests
items.takeaway: He was not impressed at first with early access, then found things he had missed.
items.soWhat: First impressions of new models mislead, so test on your own tasks before deciding.

items.title: Harrison Chase crosses out context engineering for goal engineering
items.takeaway: He struck through context engineering and harness engineering and posted 'goal engineering'.
items.soWhat: Builders are moving from feeding agents context to defining the outcomes agents must reach.

items.title: Dharmesh Shah: build AI startups off the frontier labs' road
items.takeaway: He says labs must sell tokens to recoup capex, so domain players with distribution can resell inference without being margined out.
items.soWhat: Your edge is domain and distribution, not the model, so build where labs are not heading.

items.title: Meng To: Fable 5.2 beats Opus 5.5 on a Blender rebuild
items.takeaway: He recreated his three.js apartment in Blender and calls Fable 5.2 faster, more accurate and token efficient.
items.soWhat: Early users report Fable 5.2 doing more per token, worth testing against your current spend.

items.title: AI 2027 authors now expect top-researcher-level AI in 2027
items.takeaway: Per Rowan Cheung, they moved timelines up after METR estimated Anthropic improves about 2x as fast thanks to AI.
items.soWhat: Forecasters closest to the labs are shortening timelines, so stress-test your three-year plans.

items.title: Cursor rebuilds Projects so teams and their agents share one workspace
items.takeaway: Cursor says teammates' agents can now coordinate with each other inside a shared project.
items.soWhat: Agent work is becoming a team activity, so plan for shared context and permissions.

items.title: OpenRouter, now part of Stripe, serves 125% more weekly tokens
items.takeaway: Patrick Collison says weekly tokens are up about 125% since the August acquisition announcement.
items.soWhat: Payments companies now want to own how businesses route and pay for AI models.

items.title: Matt Pocock's 'Home Repo' runs agents across many repos
items.takeaway: One repo holds skills, steering files and wiki; AGENTS.md points to clones of the other repos.
items.soWhat: A single agent home makes sweeping changes across many codebases easier to manage.

items.title: Claude now runs full apps like Adobe and Box beside the chat
items.takeaway: Expanded MCP Apps support lets app tools and embedded sites run inside Claude on web and desktop.
items.soWhat: Claude is becoming the place work happens, not just a chat window beside your tools.

items.title: OpenAI lets businesses build agents that answer customers in ChatGPT
items.takeaway: In beta: claim a business profile, manage its information, see engagement and build a Business Agent.
items.soWhat: ChatGPT is becoming a storefront, so claim your profile before others describe you.

items.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon for long-horizon agent work
items.takeaway: Built for sustained tasks in software, security and science; live in the Gemini API, AI Studio and Gemini for business.
items.soWhat: Another frontier option for long-running agents is now widely available; benchmark it against your current model.

items.title: Meng To looped a cheap model through 800 page designs
items.takeaway: Over 24 hours, each version was screenshotted, critiqued and rebuilt; he reports a $0 model bill.
items.soWhat: Cheap models in critique loops can explore design options at near-zero cost.

items.title: Gary Marcus argues investors should say no to Anthropic's IPO
items.takeaway: A contrarian essay published as Anthropic pitches investors on its IPO.
items.soWhat: Expect sharper public scrutiny of AI lab finances as Anthropic heads to market.

items.title: Anthropic launches the roadshow for its proposed IPO
items.takeaway: Anthropic says an SEC registration statement is filed but not yet effective; The Verge reports a $1.4 trillion target.
items.soWhat: A core enterprise AI vendor is heading to public markets, which brings public disclosure.

items.title: Stratechery: the Jensen Huang story gets worse
items.takeaway: Ben Thompson's Nov 10 update on Nvidia's CEO affair; the body is paywalled.
items.soWhat: Nvidia leadership risk is not fading, so keep watching your AI chip exposure.

items.title: Lyn Alden: wary of Huang's tenure, bullish on 2027 GPU demand
items.takeaway: She calls herself neutral to bearish on Huang as CEO and bullish on GPU demand in 2027.
items.soWhat: A respected macro voice separates Nvidia's leadership risk from the demand for AI compute.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

voices.quote: I built a simpler/customized/better version of @duolingo for my wife in 1 day and she loves it.
Got early access and wasn't super impressed overall. Did a few more tests as I was getting ready and...I missed some things.
I was already obsessed with Opus 5.5, but this model is something else. Faster, more accurate and token efficient.
As long as you stay off the Yellow Brick Road, it is completely possible now that you're not gonna get margined out, because you have options.

hotOnX.note: People want proof that Fable 5.2 can build a real, playable game.
Builders want agents that work alongside a whole team, not one person.

hotOnX.note: A skeptic changing his mind on a new model draws attention.

hotOnX.text: The authors of AI 2027 just moved their timelines up.
hotOnX.note: Shorter timelines from forecasters near the labs raise the stakes for everyone.
